notes:
## What it writes stays
- The **thought process** stays open at its full length while the answer is written, and after. It no longer folds itself away or shrinks to a small scrolling box. Click its title to fold it; it stays the way you leave it.
- The **answer** has its own heading under the thinking, so you can tell the two apart.
- When the app has a model try a step again (for example, it explained what to do instead of doing it), what it already wrote stays on screen and in the chat.
- If a reply stops on an error part-way, what it wrote up to there is kept.

## In short
- After a reply that thought at length, the model sums up its thinking (every step of the reply) in a few short points, shown between the whole thought process and the answer. The whole thought process is still there.
- This runs for models on this PC only, since with an online model it would be another paid request.

## Answers from what it worked out
- A model that gets stuck saying the same words over and over, in its thinking or its answer, is stopped there.
- If its thinking ends without an answer (it ran out of room, got stuck, or just stopped), it now writes the answer from what it thought, instead of starting over without it.
- When it asks for the same search again, the reminder it gets includes its own thinking from just before, so the answer it writes next has what it found.

## See how it's built on the graphics card
- On a PC with an NVIDIA graphics card, **See how it's built** now takes a song apart and reads its notes on the card: about 20 seconds for a 2:41 song, against 45 to 90 on the processor. The first time, it downloads the card's libraries once (ONNX Runtime for CUDA with NVIDIA's CUDA runtime, cuBLAS and cuDNN, 1.1 GB).
- It needs a GeForce GTX 16 or RTX card or newer, an NVIDIA driver from version 580 on, and 3.5 GB free on the card. Otherwise, or if anything goes wrong on the card, it runs on the processor as before.

## The tune follows the voice
- In Compose's **Make it real**, picking another voice now moves the tune into that singer's range by whole octaves (a song written for a woman goes down an octave for a man), and the demo is recorded again before the music model follows it. The panel tells you before you record.

## Loop and metronome in Compose
- **Drag across the bar numbers** to set a loop: playing goes round those bars until you stop it. **Loop** turns it on and off; with none set, it loops the section the playhead is in.
- **Metronome** adds a click on every beat, louder on the first beat of each bar. It's only for listening: it isn't kept with the song or made real.

## Lyrics you ask to refine stay words
- Asking a chat to refine, rewrite or fix the rhythm of your lyrics (or a poem, or any text you paste) now gets your words back, revised. Before, lyrics full of imagery ("paint the sky", "a picture of us") could make it draw a picture instead, the word "lyrics" could make it record a song, and some models asked for folder access and gave up. A request that also asks to hear it, see it or save it still does that.

## Music and Compose in one place
- Compose is now part of the Music tab. Set up a new song with any of its options and press **Write it as notes first** to arrange it in the editor, or **Make the song** as before.
- **Your own lyrics** become the song's sections, in your order, line by line.
- **Make it real** starts from the options you picked and lets you change any of them before recording: who sings and how, the language, the emotion, styles and moods, instruments, ways of singing, harmonies, the lead instrument, energy, ending, era, production, and the words themselves.
- **Several styles, moods and emotions** can be picked together, such as Country and Folk, or heartbroken and hopeful.
- Every time signature Compose offers (2/4 to 12/8) is in the Music tab too.

## A man's song is sung by a man
- Compose now writes the tune in the singer's range. A song for a male voice was written in a woman's range and, made real, came back sung by a woman.

## Fixes
- Big models stored as several files were called "damaged" in 0.9.28 and wouldn't load. They load again.

## Songs at 320 kbps
- Songs are now saved at 320 kbps instead of 128: the same song, with less lost to compression on breaths, cymbals and reverb. Otherwise they're kept exactly as the music model makes them.

## A listener for your songs
- Open a song in the Studio and press **Listen to it**. The listener hears which of the words come through, and where. It needs a speech model (Models, Speech).
- **Make the unclear parts again** remakes only the stretches whose words weren't clear, asking for a clearer voice, then listens again. The new version is kept only if it's clearer; the original always stays.

## See how a song is built
- **See how it's built** shows the song's sections (intro, verses, choruses, instrumentals) where their words are sung, and its parts (voice, other instruments, bass, drums) with their notes, following the song as it plays.
- **Edit the notes** like in a music program: click to select (Shift for more), drag to move, drag a note's end to lengthen it, double-click to add, Delete to remove, zoom in, and open a part tall to work on it. **Undo** and **Redo** (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) cover every change.
- **Hear the difference**: play the song, your notes on a simple built-in instrument, or both, with each part's notes on or off. **Keep note changes** saves them with the song.
- **Right-click a section** to have the music model change it ("bigger with strings", "a guitar solo instead"), make it again, delete it, or add a new section after it. Each change is a new version (the one before stays), and its notes and sections are read again so everything lines up.
- **Save as MIDI**: the notes of every part, as edited, as a MIDI file for any music program.
- The notes are read from the song (Basic Pitch), so they're close to it rather than exact, and editing them doesn't change the song's sound: the song stays as the music model made it.

## Compose: write a song as notes
- A new **Compose music** tab in the Studio. Describe the song and pick its **time signature** (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 5/4, 7/4, 6/8, 7/8, 9/8, 12/8, or any other), tempo, key, style, era and length. The chat model plans it (sections, bars, chords, how the drums, bass, chords and melody play, and the words), and the notes are written on the bar grid, so everything lands in place.
- It opens in an editor laid out like a music program: bars and beats across the top, the sections and chords, and a lane for the melody, chords, bass and drums, each on its own **sampled instrument** (piano, guitars, strings, organ, synths, bass, drum kits and more; the instruments download once, about 40 MB).
- **Edit any note**: select (Shift for more), drag to move, drag a note's end to lengthen it, double-click to add, Delete to remove, arrows to move by the grid (Shift and up or down for an octave), Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V to copy to the playhead, and set how loud the selected notes are. Notes snap to the bar, beat, half or quarter beat, or not at all. **Undo** and **Redo** (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) cover every change.
- Change the tempo, the key (every note and chord moves) or the time signature (the notes are written again in it), and pick each part's instrument or turn it off.
- **Click a section** to have the chat model change it in your words ("a busier bass and bigger drums"), write its tune again, edit its bars, chords, styles and words, add a section after it, copy it or delete it. Only that section's notes change; everything else stays as you left it and moves with its section.
- **Keep in the gallery** saves the song with a demo on the instruments; **Save as MIDI** for any music program.
- **Make it real**: the music model records the song with real-sounding instruments, following your notes, and sings its words. Choose how closely it follows them: closer keeps your tune, chords and timing, looser sings more of the words, so sung songs start looser and instrumentals closer; it moves in the eighths the music model uses, so every setting sounds different. It's a new song in the gallery; the composition stays as it is, so you can change it and make it real again.
- The plan fills each sung section with enough lines for its length, tunes repeat the way songs do (lines answer each other, a lead plays a riff), and the drums and bass change from bar to bar.

## Pick the era
- Songs can now be from a decade: the Music tab's **Era** (1950s to 2020s) gives the song that time's style, instruments and recording sound, and its lyrics are written the way songs were then. Compose has the same choice, and a chat can ask for "an 80s song".

## Auto picks the best model for each message
- Turn on **Auto** in the model menu (bottom bar). A chat on your default model hands a message to another installed model when it's clearly better at it (code, writing or translation) and runs well on your PC, for that message only. The chat says which model answered and why. A chat whose model you picked keeps it.

## Faster replies when they repeat text
- Chat models now guess ahead from text already in the conversation, so replies that repeat it (code being edited, a text being revised or quoted) come faster: in tests a code edit was a quarter faster with Qwen3 4B, a fifth faster with Qwen3.5 9B and over half again as fast with gpt-oss 20B. Other replies are as fast as before.

## Built for big PCs too
- **Every size of model.** The catalog now goes from small models up to the biggest open models (Qwen3.8, Ornith 1.5, Nemotron 3.5, GLM-5.3, MiMo-V2.6 and more). Only what your PC can run is shown; tick "Show models this PC can't run" (chat, picture, video and music models) to see the rest and why.
- **Several graphics cards together.** A model too big for your biggest card is spread over all your cards from the same maker; one that fits stays on the biggest card alone (faster than splitting it).
- **Long conversations on big cards**: up to 128K of context when the model still fits on your cards.
- New picture and video models for big cards: Qwen-Image 2.1, FLUX.2 [dev] (non-commercial license), Wan 2.2 A14B. Speech: Whisper large-v3.

## Fixes
- A model whose file is damaged or unfinished (for example after a copy to another drive stopped part way) now says so plainly, and Models offers **Download again**, instead of showing the engine's error.

## Fixed: sending a message closed the app
- In 0.9.26, SulcusAI closed the moment you sent a message, whichever model you used. This update fixes it; your chats, models and settings are all still there.
- What happened: Windows gives an app's main window thread a small amount of working memory, and starting a reply in 0.9.26 needed more than that, so Windows closed the app. Replies now start in memory that has room to spare, and the main thread has more to work with.

## Your own artists
- **Save an artist and every song sounds like them.** Shape a song the way you like it, then press "Save these settings as an artist". The artist keeps their style, instruments, production, key, tempo, harmonies, ways of singing and way of writing, plus a voice of their own (like "warm alto with a slight rasp", which you can change). Pick them for a new song and it comes out as the same singer. Chats can use them too: "make a new song as Nova".
- Their first song sets the starting point for the songs after it, so the voice stays close. You can also have their songs follow the voice of their first song directly (closer voice, but the words can come out less clear).

## Clearer, more natural voices
- **New music models**, each with what it's good and less good at:
  - **ACE-Step 1.5 XL**: the clearest, most natural voices and fullest songs (every word heard in our tests). Now offered first on PCs with a graphics card.
  - **ACE-Step 1.5 Clear voice**: a clear voice that sits on top of the music, just as quick as the standard model.
  - **ACE-Step 1.5 SFT Turbo**: every word heard in tests, quick.
  - **ACE-Step 1.5 XL SFT**: the richest detail, but slow.
  - **ACE-Step 1.5 SFT** and **XL SFT Turbo**: more choices between speed and detail.
  - **ACE-Step 1.5 XL Base**: adds, extracts and completes song parts at XL quality.
- In tests with the same lyrics, the standard model's voices were understood about a third of the time and could sound synthetic. If you use it, the Studio points you to the clearer ones.

## Rap, every kind of song, and songs as long as they need
- **Rap that raps.** Pick Hip hop, Trap, Drill or Grime, the Rap voice, or just ask for a rap in the description. The lyrics come out as real bars (eight to twelve words, rhymes inside the lines, a punchy hook), and the music model raps them instead of singing them.
- **Intros and outros have lyrics.** They used to be long instrumental openings. For a band-only opening, add an "Instrumental intro" in the song structure.
- **Auto length.** New songs are as long as they need to be: a length you name in the description ("a 90-second jingle"), what your lyrics or your chosen structure need, half a minute for a jingle or an advert, and otherwise the length of the lyrics written for the song. Turn Auto length off to set it yourself.
- **Fuller lyrics on long songs.** When the lyrics come back too short for the song, they're written again in full.
- **Checked across styles:** pop, rap, trap, country, rock, metal, R&B, reggaeton (in Spanish), K-pop, gospel choir, jazz and folk duets all came out sung (or rapped) with words you can follow.

## Folders belong to the chat you share them in
- **A folder you share from a chat is that chat's alone.** Other chats no longer see it, so a chat about something else won't go looking through it. Tick **Every chat** in the folder menu (the folder button under the message box) to let every chat use one.
- **When the assistant asks for a folder,** it's shared with that chat only, unless you tick "Let every chat use it".
- **Folders shared with every chat** (Settings, Shared folders, and the Desktop) are only looked at when you ask about them. The assistant doesn't open other projects' notes or handoffs on its own.
- Folders you shared before this update stay shared with every chat. Untick Every chat in a chat's folder menu to keep one to that chat.

## Faster replies from thinking models
- **Thinking has a limit.** A model that thinks before answering now thinks for about a minute and a quarter at most, at its own speed, then answers. Before, it could think for many minutes. To let it think as long as it likes, set Thinking to On in Advanced settings.
- **Less to read again each message.** What the assistant remembers from earlier chats now goes with your newest message, so the model doesn't re-read all its instructions every time. This matters most for big models that don't fit entirely on the graphics card.

## Fewer second thoughts about permission
- The assistant no longer stops to ask whether it may do what you asked. Steps that need your OK, like deleting files or sending something, show you a card by themselves.
- When you say no to something, it takes that as the answer and doesn't look for another way around it.

## Songs, in depth
- **Lyrics that fill the song.** Written lyrics now cover the whole length you pick: a minute gets a verse and a chorus, three minutes an intro, verses, choruses, a bridge and an outro. Each part gets its own number of lines, kept short so every word can be heard.
- **Song structure.** Start from a shape (verse and chorus, with a bridge, intro to outro, build-up and drop, AABA, a story with no chorus), then add, move or take out sections one by one: as many choruses as you like, a solo, an instrumental break. The length follows the structure.
- **Rhyme patterns:** AABB, ABAB, ABCB, AAAA or free verse.
- **Key and time:** pick the key (any note, major or minor) and the time signature.
- **Harmonies:** female, male, both or a choir, sung close, in octaves, stacked, as call and response or as oohs and aahs, on the choruses, throughout or on the last chorus. An instrument can play a harmony line too (strings, piano, synth pad, brass, organ, guitar, flute). With ACE-Step 1.5 Base installed, harmonies can be layered on afterwards for a fuller sound.
- **Emotion:** the feeling in the words and the voice, such as heartbroken, joyful, longing, defiant or bittersweet.
- **Vocal effects on parts of the song:** a screamed chorus, heavy vibrato throughout, a whispered verse, a belted last chorus, falsetto, growls, rap, auto-tune, runs and riffs and more.
- **Sound like an artist.** Type a singer or band and press "Use their style", or write it in the description ("Sing as Taylor Swift, a song about bears"). The song is written and arranged their way, with words of its own, and sung by a voice of the same kind (not their own voice). Their style fills in the genre, voice, instruments and tempo, which you can change.
- **More:** the lead instrument, how the energy moves, how it ends, and the sound of the recording (studio, live, lo-fi, acoustic, 1970s to modern). Songs made in chats take these too.

## Fixed
- Written lyrics no longer stop after three lines.
- The close-harmony choice no longer shows as "Close" (the window button) in other languages.

## Security
- **Safer secure connections.** Updated the libraries SulcusAI uses to check websites' security certificates (for model downloads, mail, the phone link and other online features). The old versions could, in rare cases, trust certificates from authorities that browsers no longer trust (RUSTSEC-2026-0381 and RUSTSEC-2026-0382).

## Phone
- **Your phone stays paired after a refresh.** Reopening the phone page, refreshing it, or opening it from a home screen shortcut no longer asks you to scan the code again. The pairing key now stays in the page's address (after the #, which browsers never send over the network), and the phone's password is still asked for.
- One phone can now be paired with more than one PC through the relay, each keeping its own pairing.

## Your whole SulcusAI on your phone, from anywhere
- **The full app on your phone.** Open SulcusAI in your phone's browser and use everything: your chats and new ones, switching models, the Studio, notes, tasks, mail and the rest. It all runs on your PC, as if you were sitting at it. Nothing is installed on the phone.
- **Works anywhere, not just on home Wi-Fi.** With "Reach this phone from anywhere" (Settings, Phone; on by default), your phone reaches your PC through SulcusAI's relay on Cloudflare, so it works on mobile data and other networks, with no router or firewall setup. Your own PC does all the work and hosts your phone: while it's off or SulcusAI is closed, the phone says so.
- **Private.** Everything between the phone and your PC is sealed with a key only the two share, so the relay can't read it. Signing in still needs the phone's password, chosen on the PC.
- **A PC tab** on the phone shows your PC's temperatures, how busy the processor and graphics card are, memory use, the model loaded and what SulcusAI is working on, with a **Stop all** button that stops replies, pictures, videos, music and teaching and frees the graphics card. Downloads keep going.
- **Phone-friendly:** a menu that slides in, bigger buttons, and pages that fit the screen. Pictures and songs you save go to your phone. Choosing a file (a picture to edit, a song to work on) opens your phone's own picker and sends it to the PC.
- A few things stay on the PC for safety: keys and passwords, adding or removing phones, lock and security settings, and anything that opens on the PC's screen.

## Fixed
- Pairing a phone no longer leaves a white page when the phone can't reach the PC on the local network (common with guest Wi-Fi, some routers and iPhone browsers): with "Reach this phone from anywhere" on, it goes through the relay instead.

## Pictures checked more strictly
- **The picture check reads things out instead of guessing.** It reads the words on a sign and checks the spelling, reads the time on a clock, counts each thing, and checks the color of every one of a named thing. After "remove the dog", it also looks for a faint dog left behind. Pictures that only looked right no longer pass, so the picture is made again until it shows what you asked for, or you're told exactly what's still missing.
- A correct picture is no longer failed for something your request didn't ask for, and when the reader gives a garbled answer it's asked again instead of the picture going unchecked.

## Prompt learning is now off by default
- Learning from what you make is now marked experimental and starts off. In three tests on new requests, it didn't make first tries better. You can still turn it on in the Studio under the prompt writer's settings. What it already learned is kept, and Forget clears it.

## Pictures that show what you asked for
- **Checked and made again until it's right.** With "Check the picture and make it again if something you asked for is missing" on, the picture reader checks each picture against your request and says what's missing and why. The prompt writer then rewrites the description and the picture is made again, up to 5 times, keeping the best. Edits work the same way. In tests, most pictures that missed something reached everything asked for: a sign's exact words, three suns, a checkerboard.
- **The prompt writer learns from what you make.** For each picture model, it keeps descriptions that worked and the rules that made a missing thing show, and uses them for similar requests. It's kept encrypted, never learns from incognito chats, and you can turn it off or clear it in the Studio.

## Models
- **Cancel any download.** Every model being installed now has a Cancel download button next to its progress, including models from a Hugging Face link and the first model in setup, which had none.
- Cancelling deletes what that install downloaded, so nothing is left taking up space. Files that were already on your PC, and files another installed model uses, are kept.

## Music, any way you want it
- **Shape the song.** Pick its style, mood and instruments, who sings (female, male, duet, choir or rap) and in what language, the beat, the tempo (from slow to very fast, or an exact number of beats a minute), the key and the time signature. Or just describe it in your own words.
- **Lyrics that get sung.** Songs with vocals now always have words: written for you to fit the song, or your own. Press "Write lyrics for me" to read and change them before the song is made, with buttons to add a verse, chorus or bridge.
- **As long as you want,** from 10 seconds to 10 minutes, and now exactly that long.
- **Words you can understand.** Songs are made in one pass from your lyrics and settings, with the right amount of lyrics for the length, so the singing is clear. If your own lyrics are too long for the length, you're shown how long they need and can fix it with one click.
- **Two versions at once** (or one, or three), so you can keep the one you like best.
- **Work on a song you have.** Bring an MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, OGG or WMA file (or pick a song you made), then restyle it, make one part of it again, make it longer, add a part (vocals, drums, guitar and more), keep only one part (such as just the vocals), or build a full song around a lone part. A restyled song keeps its words unless you give new ones.
- **Sound like a song you love:** pick a song for the new one to follow in sound.
- In chats, the assistant can do all of this too, and you can attach a song for it to work on.
- In the Studio, a song you open has buttons to restyle it, make it longer, redo part of it, add a part or keep one part.
- Music models are smaller to download (the standard one is 2 GB lighter) and much faster: a 30-second song takes seconds on a graphics card.
- **Pick any music model.** The model menu always shows, even with one model, and ends in "More models…". You can paste a Hugging Face link to a music model, and SulcusAI checks it can run it before downloading. ACE-Step 1.5 Base (new) does the part-by-part work.

## Nothing leaves your PC without asking
- **Anything the assistant would send off your PC asks first, in every mode.** That covers a command that uploads a file, posts data, pushes code or copies to another computer, and a request to your own network. The card says what would go and where, and it's listed under What left this PC.
- **A key or password going out always gets a warning,** even in Bypass mode: in a command, a search, an email or a message. With an online model, files that hold keys stay closed, and a result that contains a key asks before it's sent.
- **More things ask first in Auto:** deletes written in unusual ways, renames, making something start with Windows, loosening Windows' protection, asking for administrator rights and folder links. Signing in to an account, scheduling a task, adding a calendar event and replacing a note's text ask again too.
- "Allow for this chat" no longer covers deletes or sends: each one asks.
- Adding an event to your Google or Outlook calendar, and pictures or videos made by an online model, now count as leaving the PC.

## Privacy
- **Leaving an incognito chat takes everything with it:** pictures and songs pasted or made there, backups of files it changed, what it sent, and its Activity lines.
- Two settings that work like passwords (the sync relay address and the local API key) are now stored sealed to your Windows account.
- Online models no longer see your Windows account name in file paths, and phone numbers from other countries are hidden too.
- Fully offline mode now also blocks pairing a PC and every cloud request.

## Pictures
- **When an edit or a checked picture falls short, you're told what's missing** (in the Studio, in a message, and in the chat) instead of getting it as if it were done. The check now weighs what must be there more than what must be gone.
- When an edit redraws the whole scene, it comes back at your photo's full size.
- Stop now works at once, even while a helper model is loading or checking.
- A clear request ("add a black top hat") is no longer met with a question about style.
- Upscaling no longer unloads your chat model, and time estimates for edits are more honest.

## Steadier
- The mail report, meeting notes and translations no longer get their model stopped when you open a chat with another model. A model can't be removed while it's answering.
- Stop works while a long chat is being compacted.
- An automatic update never restarts the app in the middle of a reply.
- "Run now" on a scheduled task no longer makes it run twice.
- The graphics card picker explains when a bigger memory setting moved part of a model off the card.
- An engine that fails to start (often a game overlay) is started once more.

## The window
- Actions that fail now say why, instead of failing silently or showing "SulcusAI went wrong".
- Long replies scroll smoothly while they're written.
- You can see where you are when moving through the email composer with the keyboard, and screen readers name every text box.
- Plain words: speeds are in words a second, and "context window", "GGUF", "MCP" and "cache" are explained or replaced.

## The assistant gets things done
- **It does what you ask instead of explaining it.** Give it instructions, in your message, a file or a web page you point it to, and it carries them out with its tools, then tells you what it did. If something fails or isn't found, it tries another way before asking you.
- **No more asking at every step.** In Auto mode, file changes and commands run on their own. It asks first only before deleting something, or before a command that throws work away (a hard reset, a force push, stopping programs, uninstalling). Commands that could harm Windows, disks or startup are still never run.
- **It finds your files.** File search no longer cares about capitals, and when your shared folders don't have it, it looks through your user folder too (search and read only; changes still happen only in shared folders). Keys, saved passwords and browser logins stay off-limits.
- **It can go online when it needs to,** without a popup each time, unless SulcusAI is set to Offline.
- **Better with gpt-oss models** (including huihui-ai's abliterated version): their tool calls are always run, never shown to you as text; they keep their train of thought between steps; and they think at medium effort (change it in Advanced).
- Models that use tools get at least a 16K context window, and at 16K they keep their full set of tools.

## Your graphics card
- **The status bar shows which graphics card the model runs on.** Click it to pick another card, scan for cards, or see why a model is running on the processor, with a fix button where there is one (for example "Use the graphics card fully").
- **Models stay on the graphics card.** When the card gets warm, the app now takes short rests instead of moving the model into system memory, and Cool & quiet (on battery) uses the whole card. The model's file is no longer also kept in memory while it runs on the card, and models never land on a laptop's built-in graphics when it has a separate card.
- Cards without a working driver are now shown, with a note to update the driver.

## Pictures
- **Edits do what you asked.** A change is planned step by step, checked afterwards, and made again when something's missing. Moving or lifting something no longer leaves a second copy behind, and the rest of your photo stays exactly as it was, at its full size.
- **Questions first, when needed.** If a request leaves something open that would change the picture (which person you mean, what a sign should say), you're asked first, in chats and in the Studio. Turn it off with "Ask me when something's unclear".

## Typing
- **Autocomplete, autocorrect and a suggested next message** for the message boxes, each a switch under Features → Typing. Autocomplete shows the rest of a word or of something you've asked before (Tab takes it); autocorrect fixes misspelled words with Windows' spell checker (Backspace undoes it); and when a reply finishes, the box suggests what you might ask next.

## Mail
- **Draft reply:** on an email that needs an answer, the assistant writes a draft in the email's language, signed with your name, with [brackets] where you need to fill something in. It opens in the reply form for you to check and send; it never sends by itself.
- **Missed replies:** "Remind me" adds a task to reply tomorrow at 9:00. Or turn on "Remind me about missed replies" in the AI report, and each email from a person that's waited over a day gets one.
- **Invitations:** a meeting invitation shows a card with the time, place and organizer, and Accept, Maybe or Decline. Accepting adds it to your calendar (once, even if your mail service already did), and your answer goes to the organizer if you leave "Send my reply" ticked.
- **Bulk actions:** each group in the AI report has "Mark all read", and newsletters and promotions also "Archive all" and "Unsubscribe from all". It asks first when it's more than 5.
- **Lists you never open:** Subscriptions now points out the lists whose emails you haven't opened in 60 days, with one button to leave them all (you see the list first). It counts only emails you open in SulcusAI.

## Privacy
- **Online AI models in privacy mode:** before a chat goes to an online model, you see what it receives (your message, the chat so far, pictures, and what it knows about you) and can leave out your profile, memories and connected accounts. It asks once a chat, and again only if a later message is more personal.
- **What left this PC:** a new page in Settings lists everything sent off your PC in the past 30 days (searches, pages, emails, messages to online models) with how personal each was. It stays on your PC, encrypted.
- **Cloud redaction now hides more:** keys and passwords, street addresses and your name are swapped for placeholders too, and so are the assistant's earlier replies, which could otherwise go out with the real details.
- Online models are no longer told that nothing leaves your PC. Each model now knows where it really runs.

## Calendar
- Events the assistant adds now go to your real calendar (Google, Outlook or iCloud), not only to this PC, and it tells you which calendar. Invitations are only said to be sent when they really are.

## A cleaner look
- Emoji used as icons and labels are gone throughout the app. Buttons use small drawn icons or plain words, with the same tooltips.

## Privacy mode
- New in Settings → Privacy mode. Before the assistant sends anything off your PC (a web search, a page, the weather, an email, a question to someone you're linked with), it shows you what goes, who gets it, what they could do with it, and how personal it is on a scale of 1 to 5:
  1. no personal information;
  2. a first or a last name;
  3. your interests and searches;
  4. identifying information, such as your full name or an email address;
  5. sensitive information: keys, passwords, addresses, phone numbers, card numbers, your exact location.
- You share it, reword it or leave parts out first ("Share my version"), or don't share it. The assistant is told what you changed.
- Choose the level it starts asking from, and tick "don't ask again in this chat" for the level you're happy with. Scheduled tasks only send what's below the level you're asked from.
- It's off unless you turn it on.

## Mail
- **Marked read:** the check mark on each unread email is always there. Marking one read moves it to a new Marked read tab, so the next email slides up under your pointer and you can keep clicking. Undo is right there.
- **Subscriptions:** a new tab lists your newsletters and mailing lists. Unsubscribe does it for you when the list allows it, sends the unsubscribe email when that's how the list works, or opens its page in your browser. Unsubscribe from several at once, then archive their old mail.
- **AI report:** every email now gets a category: needs reply, to-do, work, personal, bills, travel, updates, newsletters, promotions or social, with filters at the top. Emails from real people that still need a reply after a day are marked Missed and listed first.
- **Reply in the AI report now works**, and replies go from the account the email came to.
- **Add to calendar** on an email reads the event from it and opens a filled-in event form, saved to your connected calendar.

## Making a model better by practice
- Practice now trains each skill on its own, mixes in some of the model's own right answers from the other skills so they aren't forgotten, and keeps a result only if it's better on the test and again on a second test of new tasks.
- On a 12 GB card it made Qwen3 4B better at writing: 35 → 39 of 48 on its test, and 32 → 35 on the second test, with no other skill worse.
- A bigger teacher model can now help with tool tasks and with tasks about your own code (it writes its tool calls differently; SulcusAI now reads them).

## Training that fits your graphics card
- Teaching and practice now leave at least 1 GB of your graphics card free. Going over could reset the graphics driver and black out a screen. A model that can't train safely on your card is told so up front instead of crashing partway.
- Training watches the card while it runs: if another program starts using the memory, it stops before the card fills.

## Also new
- The incognito button and chats have a new icon: a hat and glasses.

## Newer, smarter models
- Added the newest generation of open models: Qwen3.5 (2B, 4B, 9B), Qwen3.6 (27B, and 35B-A3B, which runs fast even partly in system memory) and Gemma 4 (E4B, 12B, 26B-A4B). All of them can read pictures and use tools.
- They're noticeably more capable than the models they replace in the suggestions. On an 8-16 GB graphics card the suggested model is now Qwen3.5 9B; with 24 GB or more, Qwen3.6 27B.
- If a much more capable model than anything you've installed fits your PC, the Models page tells you once, with an Install button. Your chats and other models stay as they are.

## Faster chats on 8-16 GB graphics cards
- When a chat model doesn't quite fit on your graphics card, SulcusAI now keeps its conversation memory in a compressed form, so more of the model (or all of it) runs on the card. Example: Qwen2.5-Coder 14B with a 16K window on a 12 GB card now writes about 2.2 times faster (34 tokens a second instead of 15) and reads your messages 1.5 times faster.
- Models that already fit with room to spare keep the normal memory, which is a little faster still.
- With no window size chosen, models that only fit an 8K window can now get 16K for longer chats.
- Gemma, gpt-oss, Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 models keep much of their conversation memory in a short "sliding window" or a small fixed state. SulcusAI now plans their memory exactly as the engine uses it, instead of assuming every layer keeps everything (Gemma 3 4B with a 16K window: 0.5 GB instead of 2.2 GB), so more of these models runs on your graphics card.

## Optimize for this PC
- Every installed model now has an "Optimize for this PC" button on the Models page. It tries a few ways of running the model on your graphics card, times each one, and keeps the fastest that fits without spilling into slower system memory. Every PC and model is different, so this measures yours instead of guessing.
- It runs by itself after you install a model that doesn't fully fit on the card, waits for the card to cool between tries, and never changes your chat window size without asking.

## Make a model better by practice
- New in Settings → Advanced → Model work: "Make a model better by practice…". Pick what the model should become an expert in: coding, writing, research, word problems, careful counting, dates and times, following instructions, using tools, or looking things up in your own code.
- The model practises tasks that have answers the app can check itself. Its code is run against tests, its summaries must keep every fact and add none, its research answers must cite the right sources, and so on. It learns only from attempts that were checked as right.
- Optionally, a bigger model you've installed can be the teacher: it answers the tasks the smaller one misses, its answers are checked the same way, and the smaller one learns from them.
- "Your code": pick your project folders and the model practises finding things in them with the same file tools chats use. Its answers are checked against your files. It skips build folders, dependencies and anything that looks like a password or key, and it learns how to look things up, not your code itself.
- Tasks go from easy to hard enough that bigger models struggle too, and practice focuses on what each model is still learning.
- It's tested before and after on the same new tasks, and the result is kept only if the model does better. Otherwise nothing changes. Works with Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6 and Gemma 3 models, on your graphics card; a run takes from about 20 minutes to an hour or more.

## Faster teaching
- "Teach a model" now trains several times faster on most graphics cards. It trains on a temporary copy of the model in a format the card handles fully, picked to fit the memory your card has free, and deletes the copy afterwards.
- Llama and Gemma 4 models can be taught from documents (.txt, .md). They can't be taught from chats yet, and the form now says so.

## Pictures

## Models from links
- Models that Hugging Face only has split into several files ("…-00001-of-00003") can now be installed from a link. All the parts download together.

## Fixes

- Models found in Ollama or LM Studio now show their capability scores even when their names differ from SulcusAI's only by dashes ("gemma3:12b").

## Faster videos

- With a model that can see pictures installed (such as Qwen3 VL 4B), each new picture is checked against what you asked for. If something is missing, it's made once more and the better one is kept.

- A chart's scale now goes past its tallest bar, and the last date on a chart is no longer cut off.

## Sites you build get real, live data
- A site the assistant builds now gets real live data (stock prices, crypto, weather and more) whenever the chat can use the web. SulcusAI fetches it for the page, so it works even where the page couldn't read the source itself. Before, live data stayed blocked or simulated.

- When a site needs a service that asks for an API key, you're told what it would connect to and what it needs, with a link to get a key. You paste the key in a popup (or say no). Saved keys are listed under Settings → Connectivity, where you can remove them.

## Settings and privacy
- Search in Settings, which copes with typos.
- Activity can be shown for today, the past week, the past month or all time.
- Cloud models: add an Open WebUI or LiteLLM server with your API key.
- Phone: only one phone can be paired, and it asks for its password each time you open the page. Phones paired before this version need pairing again.

New
- Type while it replies: Enter adds your message to what the assistant is working on (it reads it at its next step); Ctrl+Enter or Queue sends it when the reply is done.
- GPU limit at the top of each chat: how much of the model runs on the graphics card. The processor is held back to match, so it doesn't run hot instead; replies are slower at lower settings.
- Before a model loads, SulcusAI checks free memory and graphics memory, and warns you (with the apps using the most) when a game or other apps leave too little room. You can load it anyway or not.
- Chats working together (turn it on in Features): the assistant can search and read your other chats, and hand another chat a question or a piece of work. Incognito chats are never included.
- Fully offline (status bar): nothing goes out at all, except what you choose to keep.
- Paired phones can keep working while SulcusAI is locked, if you turn that on (Settings, Phone).

Safety and fixes
- API keys only go over https, or to this PC itself, and cloud requests never follow a redirect that would send a key somewhere else.
- The web tools can't be steered into your home network by a redirect or an address that changes.
- Undo backups stay under 2 GB, leftovers from a crash (including plain-text training data from an interrupted model training) are cleaned up at start, and the model's log files can't grow without limit.
- Faster steps: the instructions and tool list are measured once instead of at every step.
- Security updates for two libraries (rustls, quick-xml).

Good to know: commands the assistant runs (once you approve them, or in Bypass mode) are programs running as you. SulcusAI blocks the riskiest kinds, but an approved command can still reach files outside your shared folders and the network.

Safety
- Commands the assistant runs can no longer use up your PC's memory or start endless processes. They run at lower priority, and they stop by themselves if your disk gets nearly full.
- The assistant refuses commands that work on disks, how Windows starts, backups or Windows security, and commands that plainly delete or overwrite files outside the folders you share. This is a safety net, not a sandbox: a command you approve runs as your own program and can still reach other files and the network, so read it before you say yes.
- Model downloads pause when your disk gets nearly full (SulcusAI always leaves 2 GB free), and SulcusAI saves its own files so a crash can't leave them half-written.
- Updates now install by themselves when SulcusAI isn't busy (Settings, Updates to turn this off).
- Fixes a freeze in 0.9.1 that could happen while connecting with someone in People.

New
- When it needs a folder, the assistant asks in a popup (you can pick another), then builds, runs and opens what you asked for instead of only showing the code. You can also let it use anything on your Desktop.
- People: codes don't expire. Choose how many people each code works for, see who connected, and remove or block them. Connecting shows each step and why it failed, and checks Windows Firewall.
- The suggested model fits your PC, plus five bigger models for 16-24 GB graphics cards.
- Graphics card usage and temperature in the bottom bar.
- Testing a model shows how long it's taking and that it stops by itself.

- People (turn it on in Features): link with someone else's SulcusAI by a code and chat directly. Messages and files go straight between your PCs, encrypted, never to a model. Works on the same network, or over Radmin VPN, Tailscale or ZeroTier.
- Share a chat with people you're linked with: they watch it live and read-only, with replies as they're written.
- Assistants working together: your assistant can ask theirs a question, or the two can work something out, like a meeting time. Each side uses its own model and only what its owner allows, after they approve.
- Not on the same network? Let someone use your own relay (Cloud level), and messages and questions go through it, sealed.
- Context window: click the meter at the top of a chat to see what's filling it, pick a bigger window, or compact the chat (also /compact). Long chats compact themselves.
- Downloads: pause, resume and cancel model downloads; a paused download keeps its progress, even across restarts.
- Models: a switch to also show models this PC can't run, each with the reason, and an Install anyway that asks first.

- Hugging Face on the Models page: search and install models people share. Only the versions this PC can run are shown, with the best fit marked.
- Add models from a folder, and rename any model (only the name shown in SulcusAI changes).
- Speed test under the hardware, with a progress bar that keeps going when you leave the page; each model's measured speed appears as soon as it's tested.
- Private connection (Settings): web searches, page reads and update checks can go through built-in Tor or your own proxy/VPN, so sites see another address. Mail and model downloads can go that way too (off by default).
- When web access is off and the assistant needs it, it asks in a popup; allow it and the same reply carries on.
- Chats: scroll freely while a reply is being written, and chats name themselves with models that think first (like gpt-oss).
- Settings: the sidebar becomes quick links to every section, with a Back button.
- Folders inside Windows, Program Files or ProgramData can be shared after a warning.
- Fixes: filter chips on the Models, Activity and Notes pages; the Web menu's text running past its edge; update checks now answer next to the button instead of in a pop-up.

**Updates reach everyone**
- SulcusAI now checks for updates even when set to Offline (it only asks GitHub for the latest version number), and there's a Check for updates button at the bottom that says exactly what it sends.
- New: Install updates automatically (Settings > About), off by default. Updates install once nothing is running, then SulcusAI restarts.
- If your copy never offered this update: open Settings > About > Check for updates once.

**Mail**
- Read, unread, archive and delete now sync back to Gmail and Outlook (queued while offline), and changes made on your phone come back.
- Archive and Delete buttons on each message.
- Sort new mail automatically (optional): new mail is sorted as it arrives, with a notification when something needs you. The AI report shows the past week.

**Models**
- Speed on this PC: test each model's speed (writing and reading) and compare it with the models you could install. Test all at once.
- Choose the drive or folder your models are saved on.
- Click the model name at the bottom to switch the default model.

**Other**
- The AI's sorting reasons and the assistant's step names follow the app's language.

**New look**
- Light, Dark and OLED black (true black) looks, or follow Windows: Settings > Appearance, or the menu at the bottom of the sidebar.
- Colors from the logo, with simple black buttons edged in violet.

**Mail**
- Laid out like webmail: folders (Inbox, Unread, Sent, All mail), a big search bar, rows with avatars, bold unread mail, mark read or unread, Reply and Forward, and a compose window at the bottom right.
- Sort unread: your AI reads your unread mail and marks newsletters, promotions and notices that need nothing as read. The AI report shows what it kept for you and why (with a suggested next step), and what it marked read, and anything can be undone.

**Calendar**
- Day, Week and Month views, a small month for jumping to a date, calendars you can hide, and click a time to add an event there.

**The assistant**
- Looks things up instead of asking: if a model asks you for details, says it can't access your mail or calendar, or tells you to use a tool, it now does the lookup itself.
- No more loops or long waits: long emails and pages are trimmed to fit the model, repeated lookups and replies stuck on one line are stopped, and tool calls that smaller models write as text now run.
- Knows the app: it can tell you which email and calendar accounts are connected, connect Gmail, Outlook or a calendar for you (it asks first, then opens the sign-in page), and open a page in the app.
- Replies keep going when you leave a chat, and reopening the chat shows the answer so far.
- Email search understands requests like my

The window can no longer freeze while a page loads: every request now runs in the background. Sign in with Microsoft (Outlook.com, Hotmail) now works out of the box for Mail and Calendar; Sign in with Google works for testers while Google reviews the app. Settings shows whether each sign-in is ready.
Fixes the app freezing (white window, not responding) after opening the Studio page. Recommended for everyone on 0.8.0 or 0.8.1.

Teaching a model, quick-ask screenshots and browser control through the extension now work on macOS and Linux. Music works on Linux. Outlook calendars use the right time zone on macOS and Linux. On Linux, the AI engines stop when the app quits, even after a crash.

Sync between your PCs on the same network (pair with a code; chats, projects, memory, notes, tasks and About you stay in step, encrypted end to end), copy models from another PC instead of downloading again, and optional syncing through your own relay when away (Cloud level). Phone companion: use SulcusAI from your phone's browser on the same Wi-Fi. The app in Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Chinese and Japanese. Cloud pictures, video and voices at the Cloud level with your own keys. Music about twice as fast on a graphics card. Move models to another drive. Everything new is off until you turn it on; the app still starts Offline and runs on this PC's models.

Teach a model on your own PC (Settings > Advanced > Model work): pick chats or a file of examples and your graphics card teaches a Qwen3, Gemma or Llama model your style; it appears in the model menu as 'model + name'. Video clips now show a still in the gallery. Outlook all-day events land on the right day. Faster startup and better keyboard and screen-reader support. Copies of 0.7.0 can install this from Settings > About.

First release with automatic, signed updates: from now on SulcusAI can update itself (Settings > About).

New since 0.5:
- Backups: one password-protected file with your chats, notes, settings, pictures and meeting recordings (Settings > Backup and restore), plus a Markdown export.
- Use models you already have from Ollama, LM Studio, Hugging Face, Jan or GPT4All, without downloading them again.
- Cloud models with your own API keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter and others), only at the Cloud level, with a monthly budget and personal details hidden.
- Advanced mode: model tuning, guardrails, how it processes, and a parental PIN.
- A local, OpenAI-compatible API server for other programs on your PC.
- Clearer model status, and fixes for setup.

Install SulcusAI_0.7.0_x64-setup.exe over your current version; later versions will arrive by themselves.
